title: fix(pm): the proxy re-exec guard is the CALLER’s name, and it speaks when it suppresses
body:
Fixes #18939

Clause-②: no

`skip-changeset`: the whole diff is `scripts/pm/**` (PM loop tooling). Nothing in any
package's `files[]` moves, so nothing publishes.

## What was wrong

`proxyRearmPlan` (`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`) read **one hard-coded** guard
variable — `OS_HALF_STATES_PROXY_REARMED`, this file's own — while every consumer sets
its **own** name on the child it re-execs. So any sibling instrument's guard, once
inherited, answered "already re-armed" for a tool that had **never** re-armed. The
suppressed run then took the bypassed route and answered **401 Bad credentials** on
every endpoint, `/rate_limit` included — a self-consistent story about a dead
credential, and the recorded cost of reading it as one is about an hour spent treating
a live channel as dead.

Two separate halves, and the second one is the expensive one:

1. the guard **name** was shared where it should have been per-caller;
2. the suppression was **silent** — `rearm: false, hint: false` prints nothing at any
   consumer, so the run log carried no line pointing at the cause.

## The fix

```js
proxyRearmPlan({ env, execArgv, flagSupported, guard = PROXY_REARM_GUARD })
//   -> { rearm, hint, flag?, guarded?, reason }
```

- `guard` is a parameter defaulting to this file's own name. A caller passes the
  variable it actually sets, so only its own guard can stop its own re-exec.
- The guard branch returns `hint: true` and `guarded: guard`, and its `reason` names
  the variable, the proxy and the 401 it would otherwise be mistaken for. `hint` is the
  one branch **every** consumer already prints, so the silence is gone repo-wide —
  including for the nine consumers this PR does not edit.
- That branch can only fire on the anomaly: a real re-exec's child carries
  `--use-env-proxy` in its `execArgv` and is answered by the `routed` branch above it,
  never by this one.
- `post-stamped.mjs`, `label-write.mjs` and `board-snapshot.mjs` each pass
  `guard: PROXY_REARM_GUARD` and drop the own-guard `if` that sat **after**
  `if (!plan.rearm) return null;` — it was never reached for this defect and is now the
  plan's own branch. Their child env is unchanged: each still sets its own name.

⛔ No behaviour change where no proxy is configured. On a GitHub Actions runner the
`no HTTPS_PROXY` branch returns first, so no child is spawned and no extra word is
printed; re-pinned in both directions.

## A/B — measured, same box, same minute, `--dry-run`, no write

Exit codes captured redirect-then-`$?`, never across a pipe. No token is printed by any
of these.

**Before** (`26c73fb4e`), the card's own repro, reproduced here:

```
$ node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --issue 18932 --add finding --dry-run
ℹ️  re-exec with --use-env-proxy: HTTPS_PROXY is set (http://127.0.0.1:37101) and node's fetch does not read it.
[…] ① 取现集 — objectstack-ai/objectstack#18932 (open) carries 3 label(s) …
CONTROL_EXIT=0

$ OS_HALF_STATES_PROXY_REARMED=1 node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs   (same args)
[…] ① read — COULD NOT READ: GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/18932 -> HTTP 401 (Bad credentials)
PREREQUISITE NOT MET …  ⛔ NOT MEASURED
PROBE_EXIT=3        ← and not one line said why
```

**After** (`e424b1cf9`), the same two commands plus the own-guard leg:

```
$ node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs   (same args)
ℹ️  re-exec with --use-env-proxy: HTTPS_PROXY is set (http://127.0.0.1:37101) …
AFTER_CONTROL_EXIT=0

$ OS_HALF_STATES_PROXY_REARMED=1 node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs   (same args)
ℹ️  re-exec with --use-env-proxy: HTTPS_PROXY is set (http://127.0.0.1:37101) …
[…] ① 取现集 — objectstack-ai/objectstack#18932 (open) carries 3 label(s) …
AFTER_SHARED_EXIT=0     ← the sibling's guard no longer suppresses this tool

$ OS_LABEL_WRITE_PROXY_REARMED=1 node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs   (same args)
ℹ️  OS_LABEL_WRITE_PROXY_REARMED=1 is set and this process is NOT routed through
    http://127.0.0.1:37101, so the one re-exec this run allows was already spent and
    every request below bypasses the proxy — if they answer 401 Bad credentials, that
    inherited guard is why, and unsetting OS_LABEL_WRITE_PROXY_REARMED is the fix
    rather than a new token. A refusal below may be about the route, not this container.
[…] ① read — COULD NOT READ: … -> HTTP 401 (Bad credentials)
AFTER_OWN_EXIT=3        ← still exit 3, but the cause is now the FIRST line on stderr
```

And the half that needed no edit — an **unedited** consumer, `sweep-stale-finding.mjs`:

```
$ OS_HALF_STATES_PROXY_REARMED=1 node scripts/pm/sweep-stale-finding.mjs --dry-run
ℹ️  OS_HALF_STATES_PROXY_REARMED=1 is set and this process is NOT routed through … 401 …
sweep-stale-finding: PREREQUISITE NOT MET — GET /repos/…/issues?… -> HTTP 401
EXIT=3
```

Its re-exec is still suppressed (it passes no `guard` — see the table), but it is no
longer suppressed **in silence**, which is what the triage asked the deliverable to
contain.

⛔ Not measured, and not claimed: whether a real seat's process actually inherits one of
these variables from a sibling. The card flagged that as unmeasured and it stays
unmeasured — every leg above sets the variable by hand.

## The 13 consumers, read at `26c73fb4e`

`git grep -l proxyRearmPlan scripts` lists 14 files; one of them defines the plan, so 13
consume it. Only the three in the first row are edited.

| consumer | shape | after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pm/post-stamped.mjs`, `pm/label-write.mjs`, `pm/board-snapshot.mjs` | own guard name, `process.env` handed to the plan raw | **edited** — each passes its own `guard`; cross-suppression gone, and a suppressing guard speaks |
| `check-single-claim-paths.mjs` (`proxyPlanEnv()`), `pm/check-expected-skips.mjs`, `pm/check-prior-rulings.mjs` | map their own name **onto** the shared default, then call | unchanged and still correct — the default is untouched, pinned in this PR from the plan's side; they gain the loud line for free |
| `pm/changeset-deadline-census.mjs`, `pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`, `pm/sweep-closed-cards.mjs`, `pm/sweep-stale-finding.mjs` | own guard name, `process.env` raw — **the same live defect** | **not edited** (out of this card's ruled surface): still cross-suppressible, but no longer silently. Filed as a finding |
| `check-issue-citations.mjs` | calls the plan for refusal **text** only; never re-execs | unaffected |
| `pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` (declares a second plan of the same name), `pm/ci-failure.mjs` (imports it) | a separate implementation reading `OS_GOVERNED_MERGES_PROXY_REARMED`, shared across those two files | untouched by this PR; the same one-name-two-scripts shape one layer over. Filed as a finding |

## Self-test counts, before / after

| file | cases | batteries | floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pm/check-half-states.mjs` | 4963 → **4975** | 6 → 6 (new cases are unbatteried `t()`) | 6 → 6, every battery pin holds |
| `pm/post-stamped.mjs` | 349 → **360** | 13 → **14** | 13 → 13 (held, see below) |
| `pm/label-write.mjs` | 64 → **75** | 8 → **9** | 8 → **9** |
| `pm/board-snapshot.mjs` | 145 → **156** | 11 → **12** | 10 → **12** (it had drifted below its own roster) |

`post-stamped`'s `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` line sits inside PR #18934's open hunk range,
so it is deliberately **not** touched: the roster rises to 14 while the pinned floor
holds at 13. Both sides stay green whichever lands first, and #18934's own bump to 14
still applies. Every new battery is declared, registered and floored.

Each of the three callers gains the same battery — *the re-exec guard: the name this
tool sets, and the patrol name that must not silence it* — pinning: this tool's guard is
not the patrol's; the patrol literal pinned there **is** the plan's default (so renaming
the shared constant reds the pin instead of leaving a phantom); a proxied run with no
guard re-execs; its own guard suppresses; the patrol's does not; the suppression prints
a line naming the variable and the 401; the runner leg is unchanged; and two structural
properties — the dispatch really hands the plan this file's guard, and the plan is
imported rather than restated.

## Reader test

A seat whose parent process leaked `OS_HALF_STATES_PROXY_REARMED=1` runs `label-write`
and reads its **banner**, not a 401 story. If the leaked variable is instead that tool's
*own* guard, the seat still gets exit 3 — correctly, the re-exec really was spent — but
the first line on stderr names the variable and says unsetting it is the fix, so nobody
goes looking for a new token.

## Acceptance notes

Noted while reading the surface, ⛔ not fixed here (outside this card's ruled surface),
reported to the seat for filing:

- Four more consumers carry the **identical** defect and were not in the card's count:
  `pm/changeset-deadline-census.mjs`, `pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`,
  `pm/sweep-closed-cards.mjs`, `pm/sweep-stale-finding.mjs`. Each declares its own guard
  and hands `process.env` to the plan raw. One line each would fix them. The card
  explicitly read **0** own-guard names in `check-clause2-carriers.mjs`; the name is
  there at `:816`.
- `pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` declares a **second** `proxyRearmPlan` rather than
  importing the patrol's, and shares its single guard name with `pm/ci-failure.mjs` —
  the same cross-suppression shape between those two files, in a plan this PR does not
  touch.
- `noted, not filed:` the card's 「装饰性」 reading of the three own-guard constants is
  half right — each **is** read, by its own file and by nothing else. No carrier: this
  is a correction to a card body, not a defect in the tree.
